components.title: Motivation and Core Architecture of Model Context Protocols
components.teaches: Explain why standardized context protocols are required to decouple LLM clients from disparate external tools and data sources. Students will understand the client-host-server topology and how it solves the M×N integration bottleneck compared to bespoke API integrations.

components.title: JSON-RPC Message Framing and Transport Layer Mechanisms
components.teaches: Examine the transport mechanisms used to exchange messages between hosts and context servers, focusing on standard input/output (stdio) and Server-Sent Events (SSE) over HTTP. Students will identify how JSON-RPC 2.0 framing is used to structure requests, responses, and notifications across these transports.

components.title: Protocol Initialization Handshake and Capability Negotiation
components.teaches: Trace the step-by-step lifecycle of protocol initialization, including the client 'initialize' request, server response, and initialized notification. Students will analyze how client and server negotiate supported capabilities such as tools, prompts, resources, and experimental extensions.

components.title: Comparing Local stdio and Remote SSE Deployment Architectures
components.teaches: Compare the operational and architectural trade-offs between local stdio subprocesses and remote SSE network services. Students will evaluate factors such as local process isolation, network latency, authentication challenges, and persistence requirements.

Google MCPs → https://goo.gle/3PYkjky 
Build an ADK agent with Google MCPs → https://goo.gle/4o6h8DP 
Connect an MCP server to an AI agent → https://goo.gle/4uk7YW2 

APIs were built for deterministic programs, but AI models reason probabilistically. So how do you get your AI agents to talk to your tools and data without writing messy, custom integration code every time? Enter the Model Context Protocol (MCP). In this video, Smitha Kolan explains what MCP is, how it standardizes the way AI models discover and interact with external resources, and why it's becoming the new standard over traditional APIs for AI-powered applications
